Container.Name: Prunerr

Branch.TagDescription: Stable - the current release, recommended for everyone
Beta - rebuilt from the beta branch as changes land, for testing new features before release

Container.Overview:
Prunerr is a media library cleanup and management tool designed to work with Plex, Jellyfin or Emby, plus Sonarr and Radarr. Automatically reclaim disk space by identifying and removing unwanted media based on customizable rules.
Features: - Smart rules engine: Create flexible rules based on watch status, age, file size, resolution, and more - Automatic cleanup: Schedule scans to automatically flag and remove unwatched media - Plex, Jellyfin and Emby: Pulls library data and watch history directly from whichever you use - Tautulli and Tracearr integration: Advanced watch history analysis for accurate play tracking (Plex only) - Sonarr and Radarr integration: Intelligently removes media through your *arr stack - Seerr integration: Tracks who requested content and optionally resets requests - Grace periods: Configurable retention periods before items are deleted - Deletion queue: Review and approve flagged items before removal - Discord notifications: Get notified about cleanup actions - Storage trends: Track your library size and space reclaimed over time - Modern dashboard: Real-time overview of your library with stats and recommendations
All service connections are configured through the web UI — no config files needed.

Config.Name: Web UI Port
Config.Description: Port for the Prunerr web interface

Config.Name: Data Path
Config.Description: Path to store Prunerr database and configuration

Config.Name: Require login
Config.Description: Set to true to require a login. Configure single sign-on (Authentik or any OpenID Connect provider) with the OIDC_* variables below and/or a local account with AUTH_LOCAL_*. Off keeps Prunerr open to anyone on your network, as before, and disables the AI assistant (MCP) connector. Guide: docs/authentication.md

Config.Name: OIDC issuer URL
Config.Description: Single sign-on issuer, e.g. https://auth.example.com/application/o/prunerr/ for Authentik. Register the redirect URI http://[IP]:[PORT:3000]/api/auth/oidc/callback at the provider.

Config.Name: OIDC admin groups
Config.Description: Comma-separated provider groups that get full access, including Settings and the MCP connector.

Config.Name: OIDC operator groups
Config.Description: Comma-separated groups that may manage the library, queue, rules and scans but not Settings.

Config.Name: Local login
Config.Description: Set to true for a built-in username/password account (also set AUTH_LOCAL_USERNAME and AUTH_LOCAL_PASSWORD or AUTH_LOCAL_PASSWORD_HASH). Works alongside or instead of single sign-on.

Config.Name: Local login password
Config.Description: Password for the local account. For a hashed value use AUTH_LOCAL_PASSWORD_HASH instead (node scripts/hash-password.mjs).

Config.Name: AI assistant (MCP) connector
Config.Description: Serves the Model Context Protocol at /mcp so Claude, Cursor and other assistants can work with your library, authenticated with the API key. Only active when login is enabled. Set to false to turn it off completely. Guide: docs/mcp.md
